spans.s: chava, adj. (also śava, q.v.; Pali chava, homonymous with chava = Skt. śava, corpse, and perhaps ultimately the same word, cf. Senart, Mv 〔i.583〕), base, vile, wretched: śūrāṃ sāhasikāṃ chavāṃ (acc. pl.) Mv 〔i.278.10〕; pattrāhāro chavāvāsī Mv 〔iii.435.22〕, having a wretched dwelling.

chavi (= Skt., Pali id., skin), bark (of a tree): kovidārasya chavigandhaḥ Gv 〔501.11〕 (prose). Acc. to the English of Ratnach., chavi may have this mg. in AMg.; this is a translation of Hindi chāl, which seems to mean both skin and bark; whether the AMg. word also means bark I do not know.
